answer.policy_number: CG069 (most recent version located: Ver. 7; earlier versions Ver. 2 and Ver. 6 also publicly posted)
answer.effective_date: Not stated as an explicit date in the document text itself. Oscar's guideline library identifies currency by version number rather than a printed 'effective date' field on this document; CG069 did not appear among the guideline updates scheduled for 10/1/2026, 11/2/2026, or 1/4/2027 on Oscar's public guideline index (checked 2026), so Ver. 7 appears to be the version in force on the 2026-08-12 denial date, but this cannot be confirmed with a printed date from the PDF text alone.
criteria_quotes: Total knee arthroplasty for a unilateral knee is considered medically necessary when ONE of the following criteria are met: 1. The member meets medical necessity for advanced joint disease as indicated by ALL of the following: a. Radiologic or arthroscopic findings of advanced knee joint destruction documented by the treating surgeon and/or radiologist for ONE of the following: i. Kellgren Lawrence Grade IV radiographic findings; or ii. Exposed subchondral bone ... often designated as Modified Outerbridge Classification IV; or iii. Symptomatic angular deformity with accompanying radiographic changes; or iv. Symptomatic avascular necrosis of the femoral condyles or proximal tibia with accompanying radiographic changes; and b. Severe pain persisting in the affected knee that interferes with functional activity or age-appropriate activities for at least 3 months (e.g., ambulation, prolonged standing, ability to sleep); and c. There has been a failure to decrease pain or improve function after at least a 3-month trial of conservative treatment (non-surgical) which has included ALL of the following: i. Active and ongoing participation in physical therapy (documented) or a well-documented home exercise program... ii. Oral/topical medications (e.g., analgesics, NSAIDs, serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake Inhibitor (duloxetine)), unless poorly tolerated or contraindicated; and iii. No intra-articular steroid injections to the knee within three months before the surgery date; and d. If there is a separate request for the device, implant or prosthesis... it must be FDA approved...; and e. No contraindication present or the request is not considered Experimental or Investigational, or Not Medically Necessary, as listed in this guideline; or

2. Failure of previous surgical interventions such as ONE of the following: a. Previous proximal tibial or distal femoral osteotomy; or b. Previous unicompartmental knee replacement with continued pain interfering with ADLs; or

3. Post-traumatic injury (e.g., fracture, infection) causing debilitating knee joint destruction affecting movement, causing pain and stiffness; or 4. Bone tumor involving the knee that requires resection and total reconstruction.

CPT 27447 — 'Arthroplasty, knee, condyle and plateau; medial AND lateral compartments with or without patella resurfacing (total knee arthroplasty)' is listed as an 'Initial TKA' code considered medically necessary if criteria are met.

Contraindications making TKA not medically necessary include: Generalized infection/active illness under medical management; Active infection in the knee (unless for TKA revision); Active wound or skin infection at the planned knee joint; member has not reached skeletal maturity; known allergy to implant components. Also listed as 'not medically necessary': customized total or partial knee implant; progressive neurologic disease affecting lower extremity/extensor mechanism; chronic lower extremity ischemia/vascular insufficiency severe enough to compromise recovery; unmanaged anemia; unmanaged joint instability.
answer.appeal_deadline: 2027-02-08 (180 days from the 2026-08-12 notice date), as stated on the denial letter itself.
answer.submission_route: Per Oscar's official one-page member/provider Internal Appeal Form: fax the completed form plus all supporting clinical documentation to 1-844-965-9054. Questions or requests for more information can go through 1-855-672-2755 (855-OSCAR-55) or via message in the Oscar app/hioscar.com. A specific mailing address for member appeals was not located in the documents retrieved — the denial letter itself should also state the exact mailing address/portal option, and that should be used/confirmed if it differs from the fax number above. If Oscar's internal appeal is denied, Texas ACA members generally have the right to an independent external review (via HHS/DOL-overseen external review process, coordinated through Oscar and, if applicable, the Texas Department of Insurance for state-regulated IRO review) — the denial letter should specify this next step.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The criteria above were retrieved directly from Oscar's own publicly posted clinical guideline PDF (CG069, 'Total Knee Arthroplasty (Replacement)'), linked from Oscar's public 'Clinical Guidelines: Medical' index page (hioscar.com/clinical-guidelines/medical, formerly /for-providers/clinical-guidelines/medical). Because Oscar has published at least three dated/versioned iterations of this document (Ver. 2, Ver. 6, and Ver. 7) without a clearly printed 'effective date' visible in the extracted text, the patient/provider should call Oscar Member Services at 1-855-672-2755 (or have the provider call) and explicitly request written confirmation of (a) which exact version of CG069 was applied to this specific August 2026 denial, and (b) a copy of that exact version, per the plan's obligation to disclose the specific coverage criteria relied upon in an adverse benefit determination.

answer.notes: The denial letter states only that documentation was 'incomplete' to determine medical necessity — it does not, in the text provided, specify which sub-criterion of CG069 (e.g., imaging severity, conservative-treatment trial, contraindication screening, FDA-approved-device documentation) was insufficiently documented. The patient's appeal should ask Oscar in writing to identify exactly which CG069 element(s) were considered unmet or undocumented, and should submit corroborating records addressing each numbered criterion above (imaging/Kellgren-Lawrence grade, duration/severity of pain, the required 3-month conservative treatment trial with PT/home exercise, medications, and injection timing, FDA device documentation, and absence of listed contraindications). Multiple versions of CG069 (Ver. 2, Ver. 6, Ver. 7) were found publicly hosted; the substantive medical-necessity criteria are materially similar across versions but have some differences (e.g., Ver. 2 required 'therapeutic injections to the knee' as part of conservative treatment, while Ver. 6/7 instead require 'no intra-articular steroid injections within three months before surgery' — the opposite emphasis), so confirming the exact version applied to this member is important before rebutting the denial point-by-point.
